clue.text: Confine job to support for barrier to entry

blocks.note: to gate a pupil or student is to confine them to the premises as a punishment
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stick to propping up a barrier at an entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: To gate is the British school and college punishment of keeping someone in.
explanation.definitionFit: The upright that a gate hangs from holds up the barrier across an entrance.

clue.text: Laugh when pop concert ends with broken leg

indicators.note: a broken thing has its parts out of place, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a gig is a live pop show
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone laughs as a pop show finishes with a musician's broken leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a giggle is a light, silly, often nervous burst of mirth, one particular kind of chuckle.

clue.text: Incoherent rant on New York radio

indicators.note: incoherent speech is jumbled, so these letters come out in a muddled order

blocks.note: taken as written
NY is the standard abbreviation for New York

explanation.surface: A garbled tirade broadcast over the air in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: In older British slang a tranny was a transistor radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Tranny is dated informal British for a small portable transistor radio set.

clue.text: Slice of pork with mild pickle

indicators.note: a slice is a small portion, here just the opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of pork
light means mild, as in a light flavour

explanation.surface: Cold pork served with a gentle chutney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickle' looks like a condiment but is the definition in its sense of a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a pickle means being in a difficult situation, which is what a plight is.

clue.text: Soft and sleek, showing sex appeal? Insignificant

blocks.note: SA is the abbreviation of sex appeal
something tiny is insignificant in size

explanation.surface: Someone smooth and glossy questions whether their allure is minor.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a smooth, glossy fabric, so satiny means having its silky texture and lustre.

clue.text: Quiet reference to a British DIY home

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
ref is the standard abbreviation of reference
taken as written
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A low-key mention of a home that a Briton built for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: Prefabs were the factory-built bungalows put up across Britain after the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefabricated house arrives in factory-made sections that are simply bolted together on site, rather like a self-assembly kit.

clue.text: Feedback concerning lawsuit

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
an action is a legal case brought in court

explanation.surface: Comments come in about a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaction is a response to something, as feedback is the response people give.

clue.text: Join in league averting defeat involving Queen

indicators.note: to avert is to turn aside, so these letters are turned out of their order
involving means including, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Allies unite to avoid losing, with the monarch on their side.
explanation.definitionFit: To federate is to unite states or groups into an alliance or federation.

clue.text: Cloth rolled over opening for escape route

blocks.note: a bolt is a roll of cloth as it comes from the loom
a hole is an opening

explanation.surface: A rolled-up fabric is placed over a gap to make a getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, i.e. first.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolthole is a hiding place one flees to, a refuge reached by running away.

clue.text: Make cold cat agile after resuscitation

indicators.note: resuscitation brings something back to life in a revived form, so the letters are revived in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A frozen cat is warmed back to life, its agility restored.
explanation.definitionFit: To glaciate is to freeze or cover with ice, literally chilling something into a glacier.

clue.text: Declared name of classical composer

indicators.note: something declared is spoken out, so we want a word that sounds like the one meaning name

blocks.note: a handle is slang for a person's name

explanation.surface: Someone announces the name of a classical composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Handle as slang for a name comes from CB radio and nicknames.
explanation.definitionFit: George Frideric Handel, composer of Messiah, is a central figure of Baroque music.

clue.text: Script getting extended applause

blocks.note: something extended is long
to give someone a hand is to applaud them

explanation.surface: A play's text earns a prolonged ovation.
explanation.definitionFit: Script in the sense of handwriting: ordinary joined-up writing done by pen rather than typed or in shorthand.

clue.text: First of lovers embraced by bold sweetheart

indicators.note: first of a word means just its opening letter
something embraced is held inside the arms of another

blocks.note: daring means bold
the opening letter of lovers

explanation.surface: One of a pair of lovers is hugged by a forward partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Darling is a term of endearment for a beloved, exactly as sweetheart is.

clue.text: Stiffness shown by leading performer to child

blocks.note: the star is the lead performer
ch is the abbreviation of child

explanation.surface: A headline actor is formal and cold towards a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch is figuratively a stiff, formal manner, from the substance used to stiffen collars.

clue.text: Vegetable grown in many American states

indicators.note: something grown in a place sits inside it, so the word lies within the following letters

blocks.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second
surface padding: completes the picture of farmland across the US

explanation.surface: A vegetable farmed across many US states.
explanation.definitionFit: The yam is a starchy tropical tuber eaten as a root vegetable, and in America the name is also given to sweet potatoes.

clue.text: Set down drama omitting prologue

indicators.note: a prologue opens a play, so omitting it drops the first letter

blocks.note: a play is a drama

explanation.surface: A theatre piece is written up without its introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay something is to put or place it down.

clue.text: Ritz, maybe, hides entry to smaller quarters

indicators.note: the entry to a word is its opening letter
to hide something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the Ritz is a famous example of a grand hotel
the opening letter of smaller

explanation.surface: A grand hotel conceals the door to some more modest accommodation.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostel provides basic lodgings, and quarters means a place to stay or sleep.

clue.text: Beginnings of healthy or wholesome method

indicators.note: the beginnings of words are their opening letters

blocks.note: opening letter
opening letter
opening letter

explanation.surface: The first steps in a nutritious or healthy way of doing things.
explanation.definitionFit: The how of something is the manner or means of doing it.

clue.text: Mixed group masquerading as trolls

indicators.note: masquerading is wearing a disguise, so these letters appear in altered form

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A motley party in fancy dress as goblins.
explanation.walkthrough: Liquorice allsorts are a British assortment of sweets; 'all sorts' is any mixed collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Allsorts is a mixed assortment of every kind, as in liquorice allsorts.

clue.text: Jump over the French river - that’s a surprise!

blocks.note: to start is to jump in alarm
le is French for the
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Leaping across a river in France proves astonishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A startler is something that startles, a shock or unexpected thing.

clue.text: Entirely in favour of air transport...

indicators.note: placing one thing in another means one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a boon is a favour or blessing
all means entirely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: Someone wholly supports flying as a way to travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In favour of' reads as a phrase meaning supporting; it splits into the container signal and a word for a blessing, with 'of' as the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot-air balloon carries passengers through the sky, so it is a means of flying.

clue.text: Sudden ill-luck overcomes obdurate boaster

blocks.note: a blow is a sudden misfortune
obdurate means hard and unyielding

explanation.surface: A sudden misfortune defeats a stubborn braggart.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue one piece coming over another means it sits above, i.e. first.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowhard is an informal word for a loud braggart who talks himself up.

clue.text: ... not long ago, yet all crashed

indicators.note: something crashed is wrecked and its parts are scattered into a jumble

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: an air transport came down recently, and everyone on it crashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lately means recently, in the period just past.

clue.text: Trendy name for tavern

blocks.note: what is in is fashionable
n is the abbreviation of name

explanation.surface: A fashionable new name is chosen for a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a pub or hostelry offering drink and often rooms, the old sense of a tavern.

clue.text: Laughter from thief?

blocks.note: first meaning: a snigger or suppressed laugh, or a horse's soft whinny
second meaning: one who nicks, i.e. steals

explanation.surface: A thief chuckles.
explanation.walkthrough: To nick is British slang for to steal; nicker is also British slang for a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicker is a snicker of laughter, and also anyone who nicks things, a stealer.

clue.text: Place for artist working outside with no energy

indicators.note: with no energy means the abbreviation for energy is taken away
working suggests something being worked or processed into a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter tired out from working outdoors needs an indoor space.
explanation.walkthrough: E for energy is removed from 'outside' before the remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is the workroom where a painter or sculptor produces their work.

clue.text: Smash bits of Bee's hive? Rats!

indicators.note: bits of the following words are used, so the word lies within them

blocks.note: runs from the end of the first word to the start of the third

explanation.surface: A beehive is wrecked and someone exclaims in annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: To shiver is an old word for to shatter or break into splinters, as in shiver my timbers.

clue.text: Lean on top of dock having escaped death sentence

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: spare means lean or thin
the opening letter of dock

explanation.surface: A prisoner in the dock leans forward as a reprieve is announced.
explanation.walkthrough: The dock is where the accused stands in a British court.
explanation.definitionFit: A convicted prisoner who is pardoned or reprieved is spared execution.

clue.text: Daft sailors found in outer reaches of Solway

indicators.note: the outer reaches of a word are its first and last letters only
something found in another sits inside it

blocks.note: the first and last letters of Solway
a ship's crew are its sailors

explanation.surface: Foolish seamen turn up at the far edges of the Solway.
explanation.walkthrough: The Solway Firth is the estuary between Cumbria and south-west Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Screwy is informal for crazy or eccentric, as if someone has a screw loose.

clue.text: Talent with business jargon where souvenirs are sold

blocks.note: a gift is a natural talent
to talk shop is to use the jargon of your trade

explanation.surface: A natural ability combined with management-speak, used in a tourist outlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Museums and resorts have a small store selling mementoes and presents to visitors.

clue.text: Way round centre in Lakeland to get cargo back in

indicators.note: the centre of an eight-letter word is its two middle letters
going round something encloses it

blocks.note: a road is a way
the two middle letters of Lakeland

explanation.surface: A route around the heart of the Lake District to bring goods back in.
explanation.walkthrough: Lakeland is the Lake District of Cumbria in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To reload is to fill a vehicle or vessel with its freight again.

clue.text: Blue, sleazy haunt, right for high jumper

blocks.note: sky blue; the sky is the blue
a dive is a seedy bar or club
R is the abbreviation of right

explanation.surface: A depressed patron of a seedy bar is the right one for a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A skydiver leaps from an aircraft at altitude, a jumper from a great height.

clue.text: Progress made in West rid East of diseases

indicators.note: something made in a place comes from inside it, so the word lies within the following letters

blocks.note: runs from the end of the first word into the start of the third
surface padding: completes the picture of curing illness

explanation.surface: The West rids the East of disease.
explanation.walkthrough: The closing 'of diseases' only completes the surface; the letters are all in the first three words after the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Strides are steps forward, so making strides is making progress.

clue.text: Given protective covering in mail

blocks.note: first meaning: fitted with plating or a shell
second meaning: wearing chain mail, like a knight

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mail' suggests letters and post, but here it is the metal mesh worn by knights.
explanation.definitionFit: Armoured describes vehicles fitted with steel plate and knights clad in their suits of chain mail.
